messages:
Iris: Quick sync - proposal for a 'lateral throttle / sink' to divert noisy-tenant bursts into a cheaper degraded lane instead of 429ing. Keeps clients from hard-failing and gives operators breathing room. Thoughts? :thinking:
Ben: Sounds useful. Two main questions: accounting (how do we bill/surface) and safety (abuse vectors).
Carmen: Interface: ingress issues `X-Sink-Token: t=abc;mode=degraded;ttl=5s`. Runtime reads token and routes to degraded model kernels. If runtime doesn\u2019t understand the header, ingress should 503 so we fail fast.
Theo: Abuse mitigations: per-tenant sink_budget + a separate sink_abuse_score gate. If abuse_score > 0.5, never admit. Also emit `sink_admit` event with tenant_id for offline review.
Rao: Billing: we must not bill full price. Propose `sink_units` metric and reduced SKU, and annotate traces with `sink=true`. Lina on billing can map to existing metering pipeline.
Iris: Knobs: per-tenant sink_capacity, global sink_leak_rate, token TTL short (3-7s), sink_penalty to slowly consume tenant budget while in sink. Exempt dedicated/compliance tenants.
Ben: Failure semantics: sinked responses should include `retryable=false` and clear guidance so clients avoid retry storms. If sink path times out, surface non-retryable error code.
Carmen: Runtime work: need a fast path selector for degraded kernels, and explicit rejection behavior for old services. Add trace spans for admission->runtime.
Theo: Ops: track `sink_queue_depth`, `sink_wait_ms`, `sink_admit_rate`. Alert on sustained queue depth > threshold. Add a dashboard panel and an incident runbook.
Rao: Next steps: Carmen draft proto + ingress header spec, Theo drafts telemetry/alerts, Ben runs a small sim to measure p99 delta, I\u2019ll draft RFC with rollout gating.
Iris: Great. Keep rollout conservative: internal tenants -> opt-in customers -> beta -> general. Close sync and please file RFC.
